learning_objective: 🎯 Uncover the nitrogen-based organics! Understand how ammonia derivatives behave as bases, form incredibly colorful dyes, and play crucial roles in biology.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Amines are just Ammonia ($NH_3$) molecules where one, two, or all three hydrogen atoms have been replaced by carbon chains. This makes them Primary ($1^\circ$), Secondary ($2^\circ$), or Tertiary ($3^\circ$) amines.

Amines are Lewis bases because the Nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons it loves to donate. Aliphatic amines are more basic than ammonia, but aromatic amines (like aniline) are much weaker because that lone pair gets sucked into the benzene ring's resonance.
An exclusive chemical test for primary amines! Heating a primary amine with chloroform and potassium hydroxide produces an 'isocyanide', which has an unmistakably terrible, foul smell.

Formed by treating aniline with nitrous acid at ice-cold temperatures ($0-5^\circ C$). These highly unstable salts are chemical 'magic stepping stones' used to synthesize almost any substituted benzene.

Diazonium salts can 'couple' with phenols or other anilines to form brightly colored Azo compounds (usually yellow, red, or orange). This reaction is the foundation of the modern synthetic dye industry!

fun_activity.title: 🐟 The Fishy Smell Secret
fun_activity.instructions: If you've ever smelled fish that's gone a bit bad, you've smelled amines! Trimethylamine is the exact organic compound responsible for that distinct 'fishy' odor. Adding lemon juice (an acid) neutralizes the basic amine into an odorless salt!

exam_tips: 📌 The basicity order of amines in aqueous solution ($2^\circ > 1^\circ > 3^\circ$ for methylamines) is a very frequent question. Explain it as a delicate balance of inductive effect and solvation (hydration) effect.
📌 Remember the 'Hinsberg Test'. It uses benzene sulfonyl chloride to easily distinguish between $1^\circ, 2^\circ$, and $3^\circ$ amines based on their solubility in alkali.
📌 Aniline does NOT undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation or acylation because the basic $-NH_2$ group reacts instantly with the acidic $AlCl_3$ catalyst.
quick_recap: ⭐ Primary amines can be cleanly prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis, which avoids over-alkylation.
⭐ Because nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, amines form much weaker hydrogen bonds than alcohols.
⭐ Keeping the temperature strictly at $0-5^\circ C$ during diazotization is crucial, or the salt will instantly decompose into phenol.
